name: time-gradient-off
description: The control arm for the early-delivery bonus (2026-08-08): the game as it was before the time gradient existed, so the shipped rule can be read as a delta against it. All three seat counts are switched off together, because a run with the rule on at some tables and off at others measures nothing. HISTORY: two paired n=500 runs on the day the rule shipped, one against the first flat [3,2] ladder and one against the shipped per-seat ladder, both found this arm identical to the baseline on every behavioural metric - barn at game end 4.5 either way, game length 22 rounds either way, all fourteen assertions unmoved - and different only in the winning score, which fell 8 and then 10 points. Last-as-percentage-of-winner moved 2.4 points, under the 2.7-point noise floor, so the gradient does not measurably widen the gap between first and last either. THE AFFORDABILITY EXPLANATION WAS WRONG, and it was tested rather than argued. The first reading was that the gradient is inert because the bots cannot afford to deliver, with the instruction to re-run this arm once deliveries became affordable. The wild substitution then made them affordable - barn at game end 4.5 to 1.5, supply locks and unfinished games to zero, assertion 6 from 2.00 to 0.75 - and this arm was re-run at n=500 on top of it. The gradient is STILL inert: barn 1.5, game length 22 rounds, unfinished 0.0%, assertion 6 at 0.75, visits per turn 0.56, every assertion identical with the rule on and off. Only the winning score moves, by 10 points. THE REAL REASON IS STRUCTURAL AND THIS SIMULATOR CANNOT FIX IT. A decaying bonus rewards delivering SOONER, and ticket 38 measured the bots taking a delivery at a 97.9% rate whenever one is available - they already never wait, so there is no waiting for the rule to discourage. An agent that cannot dawdle cannot be paid to hurry. So the time gradient is not merely unmeasured here, it is UNMEASURABLE here, in principle rather than in this configuration. Do not sweep it again; the only instrument that can answer it is a table of humans, who hoard by choice.
